subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should every state-changing Gateway-authenticated HTTP route reject unapproved browser origins before authentication, or are selected routes intentionally protected only by explicit non-ambient credentials?
rationale: The report targets nonexistent or non-HTTP ACP files, while current code has route-specific and WebSocket origin defenses; choosing a generic HTTP trust policy can affect native clients, trusted proxies, plugins, and local operator workflows.

options.title: Validate and centralize the gate
options.body: Run controlled cross-auth-mode reproduction and, if any browser request reaches a privileged handler, enforce the shared origin policy before Gateway-authenticated HTTP dispatch.

options.title: Keep route-specific enforcement
options.body: Document which HTTP surfaces rely solely on explicit bearer credentials and add origin checks only to routes with an independently demonstrated browser threat.

recommendation.title: Validate and centralize the gate
recommendation.body: Run controlled cross-auth-mode reproduction and, if any browser request reaches a privileged handler, enforce the shared origin policy before Gateway-authenticated HTTP dispatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository explicitly routes Gateway and security ownership to this area, including prior shared-auth hardening. ([github.com](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md?utm_source=openai))
